text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Foreign investors bailed out of the Paris bourse yesterday, partly on rumours of polls showing the left well placed for Sunday's runoff in the parliamentary election.

-- LVMH luxury goods group threatens to buy back Guinness' participation in their joint distribution ventures, in a move seen aimed at forcing Guinness and its merger partner Grand Metropolitan Plc into negotiating with LVMH.
-- State considers buying back stake held by CDR company set up to sell off dubious Credit Lyonnais assets, in Artemis, which controls retailer Pinault Printemps Redoute.
LA TRIBUNE
-- French and German socialist party leaders call for joint programs to lower unemployment.
-- Canal Plus and media group Pathe sign agreement in principle on development in European film industry and acquisition of broadcasting rights.

-- Portugal's State Secretary for the Treasury Fernando Dos Santos says in an interview he expects Portugal to join a European single currency in 1999, says inflation and public deficit are under control, adds does not favour a flexible interpretation of the Maastricht treaty criteria.
-- Insurer AGF worried over profitability of British subsidiary.
L'AGEFI
-- CAC-40 blue-chip index fell 3.63 percent yesterday on election uncertainty.
-- AGF interested in insurance activity of GAN, chairman reiterates at shareholders meeting.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Judge investigates alleged bribery linked to infrastructure building contracts at railway operator SNCF.
-- Carmakers PSA and Renault seek to improve profitability through international expansion.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- Former Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean-Maxime Leveque remanded in custody in investigation over alleged misuse of funds by Credit Lyonnais banking subsidiaries.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- French stocks plunge on reports of private polls showing the left well placed.
-- OECD takes a first step in the battle against business bribery, outlawing corporate payments to appointed or elected public officials.
